critique: The note proves an explicit all-regime upper bound, a matched no-penalty region, a same-class sparse-nuisance converse for d at least 2(alpha+beta), and a sufficient region of polynomial separation between unknown- and known-propensity radii. It does not deliver the advertised complete sharp frontier: at the rough benchmark it establishes only the bracket n^{-2/7} to n^{-4/19}, while the dense-regime nuisance converse, matching sparse upper bound, and transition logarithms remain open. It also proves only sufficient regions for equality and strict divergence between the two experiments, not the claimed exact necessary-and-sufficient comparison map. The framing discloses these limitations without asserting a matched frontier, but the incomplete central characterization and absence of finite-sample numerical evidence for the implementable test constrain the projected leading-journal score.
